test_title: PYST 31: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 22 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What did the Supreme Court decide in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) about the powers of Parliament to amend the Constitution of India?

options.text: The President of India has the ultimate authority to approve or reject constitutional amendments independently.
The Parliament cannot amend any part of the Constitution under any circumstances.
The Parliament can amend the Constitution, but it cannot change or destroy its basic structure or essential features.
The Parliament has unlimited power to amend any part of the Constitution, including the Fundamental Rights.

solution: The correct answer is __**The Parliament can amend the Constitution, but it cannot change or destroy its basic structure or essential features.**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The **Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala** case (1973) is one of the most significant judgments in Indian constitutional history. • The Supreme Court laid down the **"Basic Structure Doctrine"**, which restricts the power of the Parliament to amend the Constitution in a way that alters its fundamental structure. • According to the judgment, while the Parliament has the authority under **Article 368** of the Indian Constitution to amend any part of the Constitution, it cannot alter or destroy its basic structure or essential features. • The basic structure includes principles such as the supremacy of the Constitution, separation of powers, fundamental rights, and the rule of law. • This doctrine ensures that the core principles of the Indian Constitution remain preserved, even as the Constitution evolves through amendments.
